title: Optimize tuner: safety checklist, rollback choreography, and post-incident playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: This ticket captures the post-incident follow-ups, mitigations, and an operational playbook for the Optimize component that recommends batching/caching configuration changes. The recent rollout of the Recommendation Engine v2.3 produced an aggressive batching/caching profile for several production routes which, while reducing token spend on synth workloads, caused intermittent tail-latency regressions and stale KV cache behavior for multi-tenant traffic. The goal of this ticket is to codify a safe apply/rollback choreography, detection/alerting rules, and verification steps so future recommendation deployments can be rolled out with minimum customer impact.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-09 at ~03:40 UTC the Optimize tuner service started applying recommended batch_size increases and relaxed cache expiry for a subset of customer routes as part of a progressive rollout. Within 12 minutes we observed 99th percentile latency increase on two critical routes (chat.generate and embeddings.upsert) and an increase in cache-miss churn due to an unintended cache-key prefix change in the recommender output format. Automated rollback failed because the config apply pipeline did not validate format compatibility, and the canary percentage exceeded the circuit breaker threshold before the remediation job completed.
timeline:
2026-03-09 03:30 UTC: Recommendation job scheduled.
2026-03-09 03:40 UTC: Tuner began applying changes to canary cohort (10%).
2026-03-09 03:48 UTC: First alert — chat.generate p99 latency up 60ms above baseline.
2026-03-09 03:50 UTC: Embeddings.upsert error rate increased due to malformed cache keys.
2026-03-09 03:53 UTC: Automated rollback attempted but failed due to incompatible config diff format.
2026-03-09 04:02 UTC: Manual abort of rollout and emergency revert applied; degraded traffic restored by 04:05 UTC.
2026-03-10: Begin incident analysis and reproduce locally.
root_causes: 1) Recommender emitted a cache key prefix transformation in the serialized config without a compatibility flag. 2) Apply pipeline performed a single-phase replace rather than a two-phase commit with a dry-run validation step. 3) Circuit breaker thresholds were misaligned with canary ramping schedule and did not trigger fast enough due to aggregation latency in the alerting pipeline.
mitigations:
Short-term: 1) Block all recommend-driven cache-key format changes until compatibility checks are added. 2) Disable automatic global rollouts; only allow canary <=5% with manual approval. 3) Patch apply pipeline to validate serialized config format and run a dry-run against a replay traffic harness before apply.
Medium-term: 1) Implement two-phase config apply (staging + promote) with automated compatibility tests. 2) Add per-route latency guardrail that aborts rollouts if p95 latency increases by >20% for two consecutive 1m buckets. 3) Instrument recommender to include explicit compatibility metadata and schema versioning.
Long-term: 1) Extend Optimize UI to simulate expected cost/latency tradeoffs given historical distribution. 2) Build continuous fuzzing of recommender outputs against runtime validators.
rollback_playbook:
1) Detection: Pager alert 'optimize.tuner.p99_regression' or 'optimize.cache.errors' triggers immediate review.
2) Triage: On-call verifies alert and checks canary cohorts via Grafana (route-level p95/p99, error-rate, cache-miss).
3) Isolate: Pause recommender apply job: `kubectl scale --replicas=0 deploy/optimize-recommender` and block future wave releases in the release controller.
4) Revert: Use the last-known-good config snapshot: `ci/infra/promote-config --env=prod --from=snapshots/optimize-YYYYMMDD-<hash>` (docs link in ticket). If promote-config fails, run the emergency revert script `scripts/optimize-revert.sh --force` and notify infra.
5) Verify: Run smoke harness against impacted routes for 15 minutes; confirm p95/p99 back to baseline and cache hit ratio restored.
6) Post-incident: Create a postmortem, schedule retro with Recommender and Runtime teams, and escalate to PM for customer communications if SLA impact is confirmed.
decisions:
- Stop all auto-accept of recommendation schema changes; require a 'schema:compatible' flag.
- Require dry-run harness pass for any change that touches cache key logic or increases batch size beyond historical 95th percentile.
- Canary defaults set to 5% with a 30m observation window unless override is approved by a runtime lead.
- Add an automated rollback job that will perform a staged revert if p95 latency exceeds threshold for two consecutive 1m windows.
followups: ENG-24601: Add schema compatibility checks to recommender output and require version tag
ENG-24622: Implement two-phase apply workflow in the config controller
ENG-24645: Add dry-run replay harness to CI for recommenders (route-level traffic simulation)
ENG-24660: Tune circuit breaker and alert aggregation latencies for canary-based rollouts
PM-402: Update customer communication template for Optimize incidents
